title: Gastroenteritis and dehydration
stem: Paediatric area. Wing, 2 years (12 kg), has had diarrhoea and vomiting for 3 days. She is lethargic, with sunken eyes and cool hands. HR 160, CRT 4 s, RR 32, temperature 37.9 °C. Glucose 3.4. Assess her hydration and manage her.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on; how dehydrated is she? Is she shocked?

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Access, a bolus for her weight, her glucose, then reassess.

review.text: Fluid bolus size. Your notes (WETFLAGS) use 20 mL/kg. RCUK and NICE NG29 now use 10 mL/kg boluses, reassessing after each.

notes:
Checked against NICE CG84 (Diarrhoea and vomiting caused by gastroenteritis in under 5s, updated 2017/2022), RCUK paediatric life support (fluid boluses) and NICE NG29 (IV fluids in children).

NICE CG84 grades: no clinical dehydration; clinical dehydration (red flags: appears unwell or deteriorating, altered responsiveness, sunken eyes, tachycardia, tachypnoea, reduced skin turgor); clinical shock (decreased consciousness, pale/mottled, cold extremities, tachycardia, tachypnoea, weak pulses, CRT over 3 s, hypotension). Shock: 10 mL/kg 0.9% saline (or balanced crystalloid) bolus over 5–10 minutes (NICE NG29 now 10 mL/kg; CG84 said 20 mL/kg), reassess, repeat; then IV rehydration: deficit (100 mL/kg if shocked at presentation, else 50 mL/kg) plus maintenance (Holliday–Segar: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 for the next 10, 20 thereafter), with 0.9% saline plus 5% glucose; check U&E and glucose. Without shock: oral rehydration solution (50 mL/kg over 4 hours plus maintenance), by NG tube if refused. Hypoglycaemia: 2 mL/kg 10% glucose. Red flags for other diagnoses: bilious vomiting, blood in stool, high fever, abdominal distension, meningism.

Your notes (WETFLAGS 20 mL/kg medical fluid) differ: current RCUK/NICE NG29 use 10 mL/kg boluses.

Perfect script checked against NICE CG84/NG29 and APLS, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (20 mL/kg, 50% glucose, loperamide, maintenance only, hypotonic fluid). Added reassessment and the explanation.

Bedside checks (pulse, ABCDE, reassessment) are done at the patient, with close-ups, not said to the nurse.

opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: Assess dehydration
steps.hint: Appearance, responsiveness, eyes, mucosa, CRT, pulses, skin turgor, urine output, weight.

General.t: Her eyes and mouth: sunken? Tears?
General.r: Sunken eyes, dry mouth, no tears.

Circulation.t: Capillary refill, peripheral pulses and how warm her hands are
Circulation.r: CRT 4 s, weak pulses, cool hands. "Clinical shock from dehydration."

Other.t: Wet nappies, blood in the stool, green vomit? And her abdomen
Other.r: One wet nappy in 18 hours; no blood; vomit not green; abdomen soft.
Other.mark: Checks urine output and red flags for other diagnoses

opts.t: IV access, IO if difficult; U&E, glucose and a gas.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Shocked: a bolus for 12 kg, and treat the low glucose.

steps.label: Reassess her
steps.hint: After the bolus; recheck the glucose.

After the bolus.t: Reassess after the bolus: heart rate, refill, alertness
After the bolus.r: HR 142, CRT 3 s, more alert. "Better, still dehydrated: no second bolus needed yet."

Glucose.r: Glucose 6.0 mmol/L. U&E sent: Na 138, K 3.6.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Then rehydration: deficit plus maintenance over 24 hours, isotonic.

opts.t: 0.9% saline with 5% glucose 100 mL/h (deficit 1200 + maintenance 1100 mL over 24 h)

steps.label: Talk to her mother
steps.hint: What is wrong; the drip; staying in.

opts.t: Wing has lost a lot of fluid from the vomiting and diarrhoea, enough to make her circulation weak and her sugar low. We've given fluid and sugar into the vein, and she'll stay on a drip overnight while we check her blood salts.

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2. She's 12 kg.
Her appearance and responsiveness. Her eyes and mouth: sunken? Tears? Capillary refill, peripheral pulses and how warm her hands are. Clinical shock from dehydration.
script.do: Lethargic, responds to voice, pale. Sunken eyes, dry mouth, no tears. CRT 4 s, weak pulses, cool hands. "Clinical shock from dehydration."

script.say: Skin turgor. Wet nappies, blood in the stool, green vomit? And her abdomen.
script.do: Reduced. One wet nappy in 18 hours; no blood; vomit not green; abdomen soft.

script.say: IV access, IO if difficult; U&E, glucose and a gas.
0.9% saline 10 mL/kg (120 mL) over 5–10 minutes. Glucose 10% 2 mL/kg (24 mL) IV.
Reassess after the bolus: heart rate, refill, alertness; another 10 mL/kg if she's still shocked. Recheck her glucose and the U&E.
0.9% saline with 5% glucose 100 mL/h (deficit 1200 + maintenance 1100 mL over 24 h).

Wing has lost a lot of fluid from the vomiting and diarrhoea, enough to make her circulation weak and her sugar low. We've given fluid and sugar into the vein, and she'll stay on a drip overnight while we check her blood salts.
